newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal to build new plant for Spectra Fiber.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal to build new plant for Spectra Fiber.

text.p: AlliedSignal Inc. said Monday it will build a new plant that will double the production of its high-strength Spectra Fiber and Spectra Shield material.
"The new facility is a response to the escalating worldwide demand for the fiber," said Jeffrey Leone, general manager of Spectra Performance Materials.
Spectra Fiber is used in making police and military body armour, blast containment material, fishing line, protective gloves and industrial slings.

Spectra Shield, which is the patented fabric made of the Spectra Fiber synthetic yarn, is used for soft body armour, which protects against automatic weapons, and is also used for airline cargo containers and even for America's Cup sails.

The company has not yet chosen a site for the plant, but said it will be located in the southeastern United States. Construction will begin in the fall and production, at half capacity, is scheduled to start in the third quarter of 1997.
The plant will be in full-scale operation about a year later.
The company said the cost of the new plant and the number of people it would employ have not yet been determined.
Both Spectra Fiber and Spectra Shield are produced in Virgina factories.
Three companies now have capacity to produce 2.7 to 3.2 million pounds a year of the composites used in Spectra Fiber, AlliedSignal spokesman John Mallen said.
The other producers are Toyobo Co. Ltd. and DSM NV, he said.
Mallen declined to say what AlliedSignal's current capacity is, but noted the company is "sold out."
AlliedSignal shares were down 25 cents to $63.625 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
